Coherent multi-cause forecasts with cause shares

Source: R/model-causes.R
cause_shares.Rd

Forecasts all-cause mortality with any model (total) and the shares of the causes in all-cause mortality with a compositional tensor model, so that cause-specific forecasts add up to the all-cause forecast in every draw (a Tucker4 decomposition of isometric log-ratio coordinates; an experimental method without a published application to mortality, so compare it with reconciled() separate models in a backtest):

Usage

cause_shares(
  total = lee_carter(),
  var = "cause",
  total_level = "all",
  ranks = c(3, 3, 2, 2),
  residual = "auto",
  residual_noise = TRUE
)

Arguments

total

Model specification for all-cause mortality.

var

Stratum variable with the causes.

total_level

Level of var for all causes.

ranks

Tucker ranks for age, year, group and ILR coordinate.

residual

Add a residual cause so that listed causes may cover less than all deaths: TRUE, FALSE, or "auto" (added when the listed causes leave more than 0.1% of all-cause mortality unexplained in the median cell; a residual that is zero almost everywhere would only add a degenerate coordinate).

residual_noise

Add in-sample residual variation of the ILR coordinates to the draws.

Value

A model specification.

Details

  1. shares of each cause (and of a residual cause, the part of all-cause mortality not covered by the listed causes) per age, year and group;

  2. isometric log-ratio (ILR) coordinates of the shares (orthonormal Helmert basis);

  3. Tucker decomposition of the array [age, year, group, coordinate] (HOOI) with ranks ranks; the year factors are forecast as a multivariate random walk with drift (bootstrap of joint changes) and the in-sample residual variation is added to the draws;

  4. inverse ILR gives share draws, which multiply the all-cause draws.

Shares of rare causes are noisy; smoothing the rates first (prep = mt_prep(step_smooth())) helps. In backtests on simulated cause data (mt_example_causes()), the 95% coverage was 0.99 without smoothing and 0.94 to 0.97 with it.

The data need a stratum variable var with the all-cause level total_level and the cause levels; other stratum variables (for example sex) define the groups.

References

Egozcue JJ, Pawlowsky-Glahn V, Mateu-Figueras G, Barcelo-Vidal C (2003). Isometric logratio transformations for compositional data analysis. Mathematical Geology 35(3): 279-300.

Examples

x <- mt_example_causes(years = 2010:2019)
fit <- mt_fit(cause_shares(total = lee_carter(), ranks = c(2, 2, 2, 2)), x)
fc <- mt_forecast(fit, h = 5, n_draws = 50, seed = 1)
